summary: Vilazodone is an oral antidepressant that combines selective serotonin reuptake inhibition with 5-HT1A receptor partial agonism, indicated for major depressive disorder (MDD) in adults. It carries a BOXED WARNING that antidepressants increase the risk of suicidal thoughts and behaviors in pediatric and young adult patients (age 24 and younger); it is not approved for pediatric use. Therapy must be titrated from 10 mg once daily for 7 days, then 20 mg, and may be increased to 40 mg, always taken WITH FOOD because food substantially increases bioavailability. Key risks include serotonin syndrome (MAOIs are contraindicated), increased bleeding, activation of mania/hypomania, hyponatremia, and a discontinuation syndrome requiring gradual taper.
indications: Treatment of major depressive disorder (MDD) in adults

dosage.d: Start 10 mg once daily for 7 days, then increase to 20 mg once daily; may increase up to 40 mg once daily
dosage.t: Once daily with food; allow a minimum of 7 days between dosage increases
dosage.n: Recommended target dosage 20 mg to 40 mg once daily with food

admin: Take orally once daily WITH FOOD - administration without food can reduce bioavailability and effectiveness
Always titrate starting at 10 mg once daily for 7 days before increasing
Screen for personal or family history of bipolar disorder, mania, or hypomania before starting
Do not start within 14 days of stopping an MAOI; allow 14 days after stopping vilazodone before starting an MAOI
Do not discontinue abruptly - taper gradually
If a dose is missed, take when remembered; if near the next dose, skip it - do not take two doses together
moa: The mechanism in MDD is not fully understood but is thought to relate to enhancement of serotonergic activity in the CNS through selective inhibition of serotonin reuptake. Vilazodone is also a partial agonist at serotonergic 5-HT1A receptors, binding with high affinity to the serotonin reuptake site (Ki = 0.1 nM) and to 5-HT1A receptors; the net contribution of the 5-HT1A action to its antidepressant effect is unknown.

absolute: Concomitant use of monoamine oxidase inhibitors (MAOIs), or use within 14 days of stopping an MAOI, due to increased risk of serotonin syndrome
Starting vilazodone in a patient treated with an MAOI such as linezolid or intravenous methylene blue
relative: Concomitant serotonergic drugs (triptans, TCAs, fentanyl, lithium, tramadol, tryptophan, buspirone, amphetamines, St. John's Wort)
Concomitant antiplatelet agents or anticoagulants (increased bleeding risk)
History or family history of bipolar disorder/mania (screen before starting)
Untreated anatomically narrow angles (angle-closure glaucoma risk)
Conditions or drugs predisposing to hyponatremia (elderly, diuretics, volume depletion)
monitor: Suicidal thoughts and behaviors / clinical worsening, especially in patients 24 years and younger (BOXED WARNING) and at dosage changes
Signs and symptoms of serotonin syndrome
Bleeding events; INR in patients on warfarin
Serum sodium for hyponatremia in at-risk patients

preg: There are no adequate and well-controlled studies in pregnant women. Exposure to SSRIs/SNRIs including vilazodone in late pregnancy may increase the risk for neonatal complications requiring prolonged hospitalization, respiratory support, and tube feeding, and for persistent pulmonary hypertension of the newborn (PPHN); monitor neonates exposed in the third trimester for PPHN and drug discontinuation syndrome. Consider the risks of untreated depression, as discontinuation during pregnancy increases relapse risk. A National Pregnancy Registry for Antidepressants exists (1-844-405-6185).
lact: There are no data on the presence of vilazodone in human milk, its effects on the breastfed infant, or on milk production; vilazodone is excreted in rat milk. Weigh the developmental and health benefits of breastfeeding and the mother's clinical need against any potential adverse effects on the breastfed child.
renal: No dosage adjustment is necessary on the basis of renal function; mild to severe renal impairment (glomerular filtration rate 15 to 90 mL/min) did not affect the apparent clearance of vilazodone.
hepatic: No dosage adjustment is necessary on the basis of hepatic function; mild to severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh score 5 to 15) did not affect the apparent clearance of vilazodone. Elimination is nonetheless primarily by hepatic metabolism.

major: MAOIs (including linezolid, IV methylene blue) - contraindicated; serotonin syndrome risk
Other serotonergic drugs (triptans, TCAs, fentanyl, lithium, tramadol, tryptophan, buspirone, amphetamines, St. John's Wort) - serotonin syndrome risk
Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (itraconazole, clarithromycin, voriconazole) - increase vilazodone exposure; cap dose at 20 mg/day
Antiplatelet agents/anticoagulants (aspirin, NSAIDs, warfarin) - increased bleeding risk; monitor INR with warfarin
moderate: Strong CYP3A4 inducers (carbamazepine, phenytoin, rifampin) - decrease vilazodone exposure; may need dose increase
Digoxin (narrow therapeutic index) - vilazodone increased digoxin concentrations; monitor levels
Other highly protein-bound drugs - vilazodone is 96-99% protein bound and may increase their free concentrations
interactions.food: Take WITH food; food increases absolute bioavailability to 72%, whereas fasting decreases AUC ~50% and Cmax ~60% and may reduce effectiveness.
interactions.alcohol: Coadministration with ethanol did not affect the rate or extent of vilazodone absorption; nonetheless use caution given additive CNS effects.
interactions.diagnostics: Monitor INR when starting, titrating, or stopping vilazodone in patients on warfarin; check serum sodium if hyponatremia suspected; measure serum digoxin with concomitant use.

serious: Suicidal thoughts and behaviors in pediatric and young adult patients (BOXED WARNING)
Increased risk of bleeding (from ecchymosis to life-threatening hemorrhage)
Hyponatremia / SIADH (serum sodium as low as <110 mmol/L reported)
rare: Severe allergic reactions (rash, urticaria, drug eruption)
emergency: Serotonin syndrome: mental status changes (agitation, hallucinations, delirium, coma), autonomic instability (tachycardia, labile BP, hyperthermia, diaphoresis), neuromuscular changes (tremor, rigidity, myoclonus, hyperreflexia), seizures, and GI symptoms - discontinue vilazodone and serotonergic agents and give supportive care
Severe symptomatic hyponatremia (hallucination, syncope, seizure, coma, respiratory arrest) - discontinue and treat
Emergent suicidal thoughts/behaviors or clinical worsening, especially in patients 24 and younger

monitoring: Monitor all patients for clinical worsening and emergence of suicidal thoughts and behaviors, especially in those 24 years and younger, during the first few months and at dosage changes (BOXED WARNING)
Watch for signs and symptoms of serotonin syndrome, particularly at initiation and with serotonergic comedications
Monitor for bleeding; check INR when starting, titrating, or stopping vilazodone in patients on warfarin
Check serum sodium in at-risk patients (elderly, diuretics, volume depletion) for hyponatremia
Monitor for discontinuation symptoms during tapering
counsel: Watch for new or worsening depression, anxiety, agitation, or thoughts of suicide - especially early in treatment and after dose changes - and report them immediately; caregivers should watch too
Take this medicine WITH FOOD every day; taking it without food can make it less effective
Do not stop abruptly - discuss any tapering plan with your clinician to avoid withdrawal symptoms
Seek urgent care for agitation, fever, sweating, shivering, fast heartbeat, muscle stiffness or twitching (possible serotonin syndrome)
Tell your clinician about all medicines, including MAOIs, triptans, tramadol, lithium, St. John's Wort, aspirin, NSAIDs, and blood thinners
Report easy bruising or bleeding, and any rash, hives, swelling, or trouble breathing
Tell your clinician if you are pregnant, plan to become pregnant, or are breastfeeding, and report any personal or family history of bipolar disorder or seizures
pk: Steady-state reached in about 3 days; antidepressant effect develops over weeks
Tmax median 4 to 5 hours after dosing
Once-daily dosing; dose-proportional pharmacokinetics over 5 to 80 mg
Store at 25 C (77 F); excursions permitted 15 to 30 C (59 to 86 F)
pearls: BOXED WARNING: antidepressants increase the risk of suicidal thoughts and behaviors in pediatric and young adult patients (24 and younger); vilazodone is not approved for pediatric use - monitor closely early and at dose changes
Must titrate from 10 mg once daily for 7 days, then 20 mg, before reaching the 20-40 mg target to limit GI adverse effects
Take WITH FOOD - food increases bioavailability to ~72%; fasting cuts AUC ~50% and may reduce efficacy
MAOIs are contraindicated (within 14 days either direction) due to serotonin syndrome risk, which can also occur with other serotonergic drugs or vilazodone alone
No dosage adjustment needed for renal or hepatic impairment, age, or gender
Cap at 20 mg/day with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors; consider increasing (up to 80 mg/day) with strong CYP3A4 inducers used >14 days
missed: If a dose is missed, take it as soon as remembered. If it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed dose and take the next dose at the regular time - do not take two doses at the same time. If vomiting occurs within 7 hours of ingestion, no replacement dose is needed.
overdose: Clinical experience is limited. Overdoses of 200 to 280 mg (5 to 7 times the recommended dosage) have been associated with serotonin syndrome, lethargy, restlessness, hallucinations, and disorientation. There is no specific antidote; dialysis is unlikely to be effective given the high volume of distribution. Provide supportive care and contact a poison control center (1-800-222-1222).
